title: eGFR by CKD-EPI Cystatin C Equation (eGFRcys) (2012) in Adults

content.equation:
Glomerular Filtration Rate Estimation by Race-Free CKD-EPI Equation in Adults Using Cystatin C (eGFRcys) (2012) (Conventional and SI Units)
eGFRcys = 133 * min(Cystatin_C/0.8, 1)-0.499 * max(Cystatin_C/0.8, 1)-1.328 * 0.996Age * SexFactor
BSA = 0.007184 * Height0.725 * Weight0.425 eGFRcys for this BSA = eGFRcys * BSA / 1.73
notes: eGFRcys is calculated by an equation developed by the Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration (CKD-EPI) and may be used to estimate kidney function when cystatin C concentrations are stable.[1]
To monitor and stage chronic kidney disease, eGFR normalized to a BSA of 1.73 m2 is used to allow for comparison of the patient's kidney function to normal values.

For medication-related decision making (dose adjustments), eGFR without normalization to BSA is used for patients with BSAs significantly lower or higher than 1.73 m2 (ie, small or very large patients).[2]
Calculators to estimate eGFR using the race-free CKD-EPI equations with creatinine and cystatin C combined (eGFRcr-cys) and creatinine only (eGFRcr) are available separately.
Additional GFR estimation methods are discussed in the appropriate literature as well as UpToDate topics on the assessment of kidney function.

BSA: body surface area; eGFR: estimated glomerular filtration rate; eGFRcr: estimated glomerular filtration rate using creatinine; eGFRcr-cys: estimated glomerular filtration rate using creatinine and cystatin C combined; eGFRcys: estimated glomerular filtration rate using cystatin C; GFR: glomerular filtration rate.
content.data_input_disclaimer: ONLY DIGITS 0 TO 9 AND A SINGLE DECIMAL POINT (".") ARE ACCEPTABLE AS NUMERIC INPUTS. ATTEMPTED INPUT OF OTHER CHARACTERS INTO A NUMERIC FIELD MAY LEAD TO AN INCORRECT RESULT.

references.text: 1. Inker LA, Eneanya ND, Coresh J, et al; Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration.

Moving forward from Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance to race-free estimated glomerular filtration rate to improve medication-related decision-making in adults across healthcare settings: a consensus of the National Kidney Foundation Workgroup for Implementation of Race-Free eGFR-Based Medication-Related Decisions. Am J Health Syst Pharm. 2025;82(12):644-659. doi:10.1093/ajhp/zxae317[PubMed 39552516]
